$comment: Grounds and page geometry, and THE LAYOUT MODEL as data - the three components, the width settings, the border pairs and the truncate declarations. The laws they obey are in index/laws.json. build.py validates every class against the shipped CSS and every token against dist/tokens.json, then emits this as manifest.grounds, manifest.layout and manifest.color. R23.

grounds.note: The full-bleed dark band. Same ground as 'dark'; what makes it a band is the bleed, which is layout rather than color.

paper.is: a component that carries a fill, a stroke and other components
paper.placedBy: a container, like any other component - never directly on a ground (P22)

hug.takes: what its content needs and no more
hug.minimum: none - the escape hatch is set, not a parameter on hug

set.takes: a width from the maxWidth ladder
set.note: The declared number is the CONTAINER's width, its own inset already inside it on both edges, so the text measure is the name minus 48.

width.namedFor: the container that is NOT set to fill, and which side it is on - which extends to set-left / set-right for free, and folds the one-container case in as fill and set.
width.shipsAs: data-container on the ground (equal / hug-left / hug-right / set-left / set-right); data-width and data-set on a single container; data-lead names the type role of the largest line, which the container pads 1.5 x.

borderPairing.band: 1.21 to 1.56 - this system's working definition of a visible edge that is not a line you notice. Measured on the light half; the dark half does not hold it, and rebalancing it is an open operator decision.
borderPairing.tints: No on-tint-* token exists, so a paper in a tint has no stroke the system can name. Candidate on the table: step 20 of the fill's own ramp.

truncate.declarations: min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis
truncate.loadBearing: min-width: 0 - a grid or flex item takes an automatic minimum of its own content, and without the override it never clips.

vocabulary.ink: The color of a mark: text, and marks that read as text - icons, bullets, glyphs.
vocabulary.fill: The color of a painted area. surface and action are families of fills.
vocabulary.border: A stroke that surrounds a fill, and pairs to that fill.
vocabulary.divider: A stroke that separates two things and belongs to neither, so it takes a divider color rather than a pairing.
vocabulary.edge: A one-sided stroke that carries state: severity, emphasis level, selection.
